properties.name: Reviewed: gap:8f3bacedc618f3d4
properties.rationale:
ACCEPTED WHILE PLANNED, AND NOW DATED — Anthony's call 2026-07-31, taken with the other three of its kind as one judgement.

The gap's literal question — "how will you confirm it?" — is ALREADY ANSWERED: ver:skill-triggers is written and sits at `planned`, pinning that shape-matching fires on the situation AND stays silent otherwise (the counterweight is the half that matters, since a trigger that always fires teaches the agent to ignore it). What the gap reports is that the check has never RUN, which is true of anything unbuilt.

WHY ACCEPT RATHER THAN LEAVE OPEN: these four were the only notes on the gate, so every cut printed "5 notes" with no way to tell signal from permanent background. When the capability is built and its check passes, the gap disappears on its own.

*** CORRECTION, MADE THE SAME DAY, LEFT ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN EDITED AWAY. *** This rationale originally claimed `cap:review-expires-on-content` would bring the gap back if the capability were reworded. THAT IS FALSE — that capability is PLANNED, NOT BUILT. Expiry keys on the gap id, which hashes affected node IDS, so a review expires when the affected SET changes membership and NEVER on CONTENT change. This review does NOT self-expire; reword the capability and someone must revisit it BY HAND. Demonstrated live the same hour on the sibling acknowledgement decision:ack:4f9dcb95353889c2, where a substantial rewrite left the old judgement suppressing the gap against new text.

WHY IT IS SCHEDULED AND NOT MERELY ACCEPTED: all four were scheduled against NOTHING, so quieting them would have relied on memory. Now SCHEDULED_FOR rel:v0210 as `expected`, so arrival_delta asks at v0.21.0 regardless.

A SEPARATE THING NOT TO CONFUSE WITH THIS: cap:skill-triggers is also the single `unexamined` entry in confirmation_ledger, and that is BL-108, not this gap. The ledger attributes artifacts through a capability's COMPONENT, so cmp:nudge owning art:nudge-detect makes a PLANNED capability read as an unexamined BUILT claim. An exhaustive reconcile_artifacts (98/98 unchanged, 0 findings, 2026-07-31) does not clear it and must not — confirming it would assert that something unbuilt has been checked against reality.

DELIBERATELY NOT IN v0.20.0, which Anthony scoped to cap:changelog-view alone.
